alignments.note: Construct noun with the supplied the (rules 15, 29). דֶּגֶל מַחֲנֵה אֶפְרַיִם is the definite subject of this verbless clause, so the construction's copula is not this unit's (rule 20).
Nomen rectum with the relational of and a supplied the (rules 19, 29).
Inner rectum with its own of (rule 19).
לְ rendered by the compound preposition according to, headed on according (rules 30, 24).
יָם rendered the west side; side is the ASV's supplied generic and the the is supplied, so both join the noun's unit, headed on west (rules 15, 31).

The directive he has a word of its own, On, and heads on it (rule 32). The directional phrase is the predicate of this verbless clause, so the construction's copula shall be joins it on rule 49's terms, discontinuous around the noun under rule 25. Placing shall be on the noun's unit (headed west) or on דֶּגֶל under rule 20 was available; rule 20 directs reading the Hebrew for which side is the predicate, and the definite construct phrase is the subject.
Supplied the joins the nominal it determines (rule 15).

review_notes: Corrected on the same ground as 2.10: in דֶּגֶל מַחֲנֵה אֶפְרַיִם לְצִבְאֹתָם יָמָּה the definite construct phrase is the subject and יָמָּה the predicate, so rule 20 sends the construction's copula to the predicate rather than leaving it beside the subject where the ASV writes it.
The copula is placed on the directive he, which holds the English On and stands where rule 49's preposition stands; putting it on יָם's own unit instead is named in that unit's note.
